label: Guard time per command
means: How long the bash guard takes to judge one harmless command on the machine that runs the sessions.
goal_source: Git Crafter's own goal: a tenth of a second, about the limit for a system to feel instant; near is one second, about the limit for a user's flow of thought (Jakob Nielsen, Response Times: The 3 Important Limits, nngroup.com/articles/response-times-3-important-limits, 1993-01-01, read 2026-11-10). The guard runs before every Bash call, so it is the hot path to optimize first (Microsoft Learn, Well-Architected PE:07, updated 2025-10-30, read 2026-11-10)
source: latest: median wall time of params.runs (10) runs of python3 -I params.guard judging one harmless command on stdin, in a --local collect on the machine that runs the sessions; the command is parsed, never run. Not read in CI, where a runner under load would time itself

label: Guard time per command on a cloud runner
means: How long the bash guard takes to judge one command on GitHub's ubuntu-slim runner, start-up included.
goal_source: Git Crafter's own goal: a tenth of a second, about the limit for a system to feel instant; near is one second, about the limit for a user's flow of thought (Jakob Nielsen, Response Times: The 3 Important Limits, nngroup.com/articles/response-times-3-important-limits, 1993-01-01, read 2026-11-10). The guard runs before every Bash call, so it is the hot path to optimize first (Microsoft Learn, Well-Architected PE:07, updated 2025-10-30, read 2026-11-10)
source: latest: median of 40 fresh python3 -I tools/bash_guard.py --check calls on corpus cases spread evenly across tools/bash_guard_cases.json, timed by tools/tests/guard_speed.py in verify.yml job short (tools/verify.sh, right after the guard self-test) and read from that job's log in the newest successful run on the default branch; p95 beside it. Each command is parsed, never run
